+title: Fix the code-hygiene findings of the range af04397..0774430 (agents tool and skills marketplace tests)
+---
+## Why
+
+The reviews of ^c4a6mwy and ^t87yzmg ran without `code-hygiene/dead-code-swift`, because of the orphan checkout in `.build`. On 2026-10-10 a `code-hygiene` review of the whole range `af04397~1..0774430` ran. The dead-code rule found nothing. Three other rules found these items. Each one is a requirement. Fix each cause in the whole file.
+
+## Review Findings (2026-10-10 08:59)
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/AgentsToolTests.swift:373` `reuse/reuse` — The new `makeAgent(label:inlineSettleGrace:)` rebuilds the stub agent that `makeStubAgent` already builds, then calls `initialize`. The copy repeats the router, the user directory and the defaults-layer environment. It does not extend `makeStubAgent` with an `inlineSettleGrace` parameter, so the test suite now has two stub-agent constructors that drift apart. The `makeStubAgent` doc comment says every suite constructs through it. Add an `inlineSettleGrace: TimeInterval` parameter, with the current default, to `makeStubAgent` in StubProfileFixtures.swift and pass it through to `RoutedACPAgent`. Then replace the body of `AgentsToolTests.makeAgent` with one `makeStubAgent(...)` call plus `initialize`.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ConfigShowTests.swift:89` `swift/immutability` — The `keyLines(in:)` helper keeps a mutable `var itemIndent` that the `filter` closure reads and writes on every line. The reader must walk the whole closure to learn which lines are kept, and the filter depends on the order of the calls. A `map`/`filter` over a precomputed set of item ranges would state the result without shared mutable state. Compute the sequence-item lines in one pass that returns a Boolean per line, or split the text into item blocks first, then take the key lines from the blocks that are not items. Keep the result as a `let` built from `map`/`filter`.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ToolSectionCodecTests.swift:384` `reuse/reuse` — The new test `theConfigInitDocumentReadsBackWithTheAgentsToolOn` repeats the body of the existing environment round-trip test. Both build the builtin configuration, write it with `ConfigurationYAML.documentText`, read it back with `loadProjectConfig`, and assert the text fragment, equality with the builtin, and the mounted options. Only the section name and the expected fragment differ. Writing a second copy means the two round-trip checks can drift apart. Extend the existing round-trip check into one parameterized test over the section, for example by passing the section key and a closure that reads its `mountedOptions`, and use it for both `environment` and `agents`. Keep the per-section fragment as an argument so each case still names its own key.
+
+## Tests
+
+The suites AgentsToolTests, ConfigShowTests, ToolSectionCodecTests and each suite that uses `makeStubAgent` pass. The full root suite passes. These are refactors of tests that already pass, so each test must still pass after the change.
+
+#tests
\ No newline at end of file
